findings.title: Nil http.Client causes a panic on every call
findings.evidence: The function accepts a client pointer and immediately dereferences it via client.Do without any nil guard, so a caller passing nil will panic instead of getting an error.
findings.recommendation: Either reject a nil client up front with a returned error, or default to http.DefaultClient when client is nil before calling Do.

findings.title: Responses larger than 1 MiB are silently truncated and reported as success
findings.evidence: The body is read through a LimitReader capped at maxBody and then returned directly, so any 200 OK response exceeding that size is cut off with no error to the caller.
findings.recommendation: Detect overflow instead of silently truncating, for example by limiting to maxBody+1 bytes and returning an error if more than maxBody bytes are received.
